newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha rallies on buoyant crude, Skikda delay.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha rallies on buoyant crude, Skikda delay.

text.p: NWE naphtha rallied sharply on Tuesday to catch up the strong crude gains late Monday and to compensate for continued delays at Algeria's Skikda port, traders said.
One end-user was believed to be shipping material from Tunisia to Antwerp because of the delays, they said.
Dec swaps rose $3.75 to $229/$230 before easing back to $228/$229 when crude retraced some of its gains. Jan swaps were up $3 at $220/$221.
A paper offer was heard for $230 cif but not completed and there was a bid for a pipeline spec cargo at $230 cif, traders said.
A 6,000 tonne Russian cargo was on offer in NWE at $233 cif but appeared to have difficulty finding a buyer because of specification problems and the high price, said one trader.
End-user demand in NWE was generally seen as lacklustre and it was unclear how long the Skikda delays would have to last to have a significant impact on prices.
"There will be material available," from Russia, about one to two parcels each week, and from local suppliers into NWE, said one broker.
A port official said a methane carrier may be berthed later on Tuesday at Skikda and oil tankers may be able to berth on Wednesday, based on better weather forecasts.
Four large tankers able to hold 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes were waiting to be loaded at Skikda, which has been shut for most of the last two weeks due to strong winds and rough seas.
Traders were unsure if the arbitrage to the U.S. was open.
